task: Cycle 6 C6-02: Blackwell small-shape NVFP4 quantizer fusion, fused cuBLASLt alpha and wide cross-mix latency against the C6-01 perplexities

kernel_parity.reference: micro_rotated_ptq rotation (FP32) + nvfp4_encode + pack_e2m1 + to_blocked (nb.quantize_activation_ref); the packed-table cases also compare the layer output with the C5-03 NVFP4Linear bit for bit

part_a.design: Williams-balanced orders over all methods; CUDA events, mean of `iters` flushed samples per round (raw per-call times in event_samples_ms), 4x L2 flush before every sample; median over rounds. `wall_ms`: host clock between synchronizes. c5_03_* is nvfp4_inference_blackwell (pinned bytes) with torch._scaled_mm_v2; c6_02_* is nvfp4_small_shape_blackwell (FastNVFP4Linear sharing the same NVFP4 weights) with the direct cuBLASLt call; both allocate their buffers per call. Large inputs (fs.DELEGATE_FROM, fs.DELEGATE_MIN_K per rotation) are delegated to the C5-03 path by design.

part_b.design: Profiler traces of one call (CPU aten ops, CUDA kernels); the direct cuBLASLt call writes into a NaN-filled output (beta = 0 must not read C) and is compared bit for bit with nvfp4_scaled_mm_public for every shape, rotation and output dtype; every heuristic algorithm is timed as a CUDA graph (4x L2 flush).

part_c.design: random-init BF16 weights and tokens; every block linear (qkv, out, gate, up, down) replaced by an RTN NVFP4 layer. Variants: c5_03_* nvfp4_inference_blackwell, c6_02_* FastNVFP4Linear on the same weights. Wide families: c6_01_* = rotated_qat.CrossInput (FP32 PyTorch cross-block mix) over the C5-03 layer (the C6-01 hardware path), c6_02_crossinput_* the same over FastNVFP4Linear, c6_02_fused_* FastCrossInput (one Triton cross-mix kernel). One CUDA graph per forward (shared memory pool), Williams-balanced, 4x L2 flush. Embedding, norms, attention and the tied head stay BF16.

caveats: nvfp4_inference_blackwell.py (C5-03) is unchanged: the C5-03 and C6-01 validators pin its bytes, so the C6-02 fast path is the separate module nvfp4_small_shape_blackwell (drop-in, bit-identical operands and outputs).

Part A: C6-02 beats BF16 cuBLAS in 31/32 CUDA-graph cells; trailing cells: [[1024, 512, 1408, 'bfly_b16']]; non-delegated cells slower than C5-03: none. Each cell is one Williams-balanced session; cell-to-cell differences of about 1-2% are within the session-to-session spread measured while tuning (the GPU also drives the desktop).

Large inputs use the C5-03 quantizer and torch._scaled_mm_v2 by design (fs.delegated: none from 2^23 elements, the butterfly from 2^21 elements with K >= 2048, never hadamard_b16): there the DRAM-bound C5-03 2D tiles match or beat the C6-02 kernels (c6_02_no_delegate ablation at 2048 x 8192; the limits come from pre-run sweeps recorded in the module). Delegated cells run the same code as C5-03: [[1024, 768, 2048, 'bfly_b16'], [1024, 4096, 4096, 'bfly_b16'], [2048, 8192, 8192, 'none'], [2048, 8192, 8192, 'bfly_b16']]; their C5-03/C6-02 differences are session noise.

Part B: the elementwise kernel is aten::mul of the two FP32 tensor scales inside torch._scaled_mm_v2; the C6-02 quantizer writes alpha = global_scale * w_global (one rounded FP32 product, the same value) and the GEMM calls cublasLtMatmul with PyTorch's descriptor (1 MiB heuristic limit, device pointer mode). Equality with nvfp4_scaled_mm_public is measured bit for bit, not derived; it holds for the cuBLASLt build of this torch wheel. The direct call runs through ctypes (host cost in eager mode).
Part C models use random weights: latency does not depend on the weight values, but the NLL axis of the Pareto comes from the C6-01 three-seed test means (pinned C6-01 result), not from these models.

The fused cross-mix (FastCrossInput) reproduces the two-half FMA order of the cuBLAS gemmSN kernels that torch.matmul picks for most shapes; where cuBLAS picks another kernel the mixed FP32 values differ by rounding. Its parity against rotated_qat.CrossInput (mixed-value and logits mismatches) is measured per model and family, so the C6-01 NLLs carry over approximately (near-0 parity), not bit for bit, for the full mix.
Every wide-family linear computes its own cross-mix as in the C6-01 hardware path (gate and up mix the same input twice); sharing it would be a further model-level change, not measured here.
The butterfly coefficients of FastNVFP4Linear live in a non-persistent (16, G, 4) buffer derived from the (cos, sin) tables; the public quantize_activation keeps the (G, 4, 8) table API.

Study history: a first canonical attempt from a4ebc54 was rejected by its validator (part_c 50m: kernel launches per forward: delegated layers were not counted); this result was measured again after that rule and the per-rotation delegation limits were corrected. The rejected payload and log are retained outside git with the SHA-256 values in SUPERSEDED_ATTEMPT.
